assignedReviews.card_evidence: This makes you lighter and helps you float on your back in the water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe things that affect the movement of objects, including size, shape, heaviness, material, and surface texture
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains buoyancy/floating due to air in the lungs, not the movement of objects. It mentions 'lighter' (heaviness) but does not describe how heaviness affects movement, which is the focus of G3-F-2. The content is about floating, a static buoyancy phenomenon, not about moving objects.

copy.en:
Ever wonder why you float better after a big breath?

When you breathe in deeply, your lungs fill with air! This makes you lighter and helps you float on your back in the water.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas madaling lumutang pagkatapos ng malalim na hininga?

Kapag malalim ang hininga mo, puno ng hangin ang baga mo! Kaya mas magaan ka at mas madaling lumutang nang nakatihaya sa tubig.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mas sayon molutaw pagkahuman sa lawom nga ginhawa?

Kung lawom ang imong ginhawa, mapuno sa hangin ang imong baga! Mao nga mas gaan ka ug mas sayon molutaw nga naghapa sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Duckweed is one of the smallest floating plants
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a floating plant, which could imply an aquatic habitat, but it does not use a drawing or diagram to classify Philippine plants by habitat as required. It only states a fact about duckweed's size and appearance.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Duckweed is one of the smallest floating plants
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups (flowering/non-flowering plants, animal groups, microorganisms). It only gives a single fact about duckweed, with no classification or comparison of characteristics.

copy.en:
What is the smallest floating plant?

Duckweed is one of the smallest floating plants -- each one is only as big as a grain of rice! Many together look like a green carpet on a pond.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamaliit na lumulutang na halaman?

Ang duckweed ay isa sa pinakamaliit na lumulutang na halaman -- kasing liit ng butil ng kanin! Kapag dumami, parang berdeng kumot ito sa ibabaw ng lawa.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakagamay nga naglutaw nga tanom?

Ang duckweed usa sa pinakagamay nga naglutaw nga tanom -- kasing gamay sa usa ka lugas sa bugas! Kon modaghan, morag berde nga kumot kini sa nawong sa linaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The filament is the thin stalk of the stamen that holds up and supports the anther of a flower.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Filament supporting the anther is floral morphology; the card never says the anther makes pollen or describes pollination, seed production, or propagation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The filament is the thin stalk of the stamen that holds up and supports the anther
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: A floral stalk holding the anther is not leaves, roots, or stems taking water and nutrients from soil.

copy.en:
What holds up a flower's anther?

The filament is the thin stalk of the stamen that holds up and supports the anther of a flower.
copy.tl:
Ano ang humahawak sa anther ng bulaklak?

Ang filament ay ang manipis na tangkay ng stamen na humahawak at sumusuporta sa anther ng bulaklak.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naghawid sa anther sa bulak?

Ang filament mao ang nipis nga punoan sa stamen nga naghawid ug nagsuporta sa anther sa bulak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Colorful petals sit inside to attract insects
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes petals and sepals, which are flower parts, not the outer plant parts (leaves, roots, stems) named in the competency, and it does not address their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil.

copy.en:
What's the difference between petals and sepals?

Petals and sepals aren't the same! Colorful petals sit inside to attract insects, while green sepals sit outside to protect the flower — that's why people mix them up.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng petals at sepals?

Magkaiba ang petals at sepals! Makulay ang petals at nasa loob para mang-akit ng insekto, samantalang berde ang sepals at nasa labas para magprotekta — kaya sila madalas nalilito!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang kalahian sa petals ug sepals?

Lahi ang petals ug sepals! Mabulukon ang petals ug naa sa sulod aron makadani og insekto, samtang lunhaw ang sepals ug naa sa gawas aron manalipod — mao nga sagad sila malibog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sepals are the green parts that wrap around and protect a flower bud before it opens.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Bud protection is floral morphology; the card never describes pollination, seed production, or propagation.

copy.en:
What protects a flower before it blooms?

The sepals are the green parts that wrap around and protect a flower bud before it opens.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagpoprotekta sa bulaklak bago mamukadkad?

Ang sepal ang berdeng bahagi na bumabalot at nagpoprotekta sa buko ng bulaklak bago ito mamukadkad.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nanalipod sa bulak sa wala pa kini mobukhad?

Ang sepal mao ang lunhaw nga bahin nga moputos ug manalipod sa usbong sa buwak sa wala pa kini mobukhad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: at night they're attracted to fishing lights
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a specific example of a flying fish responding to light, but it does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) nor explicitly connect this behavior to the concept of response as a characteristic of living things. It is a factual anecdote rather than instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Why do flying fish leap onto boats?

Because at night they're attracted to fishing lights -- sometimes they leap right onto the boat!
copy.tl:
Bakit tumatalon ang isdang lumilipad papunta sa bangka?

Dahil naaakit sila sa ilaw ng pangingisda sa gabi -- minsan tumatalon pa sila papunta mismo sa bangka!
copy.bis:
Ngano molukso ang naglupad nga isda sa sakayan?

Kay madani sila sa suga sa pagpangisda sa gabii -- usahay molukso pa gyud sila diretso sa sakayan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dragging creates friction between the sack and the ground, resisting your pull!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a friction concept but does not involve planning or carrying out an investigation, nor does it address different surfaces or measuring frictional forces.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You just have to lift the weight against gravity instead!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gravity as something to lift against, but does not identify gravity as a non-contact force or describe its predictable effects on materials/objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dragging creates friction between the sack and the ground, resisting your pull!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes friction resisting motion but does not demonstrate friction producing heat or investigate ways of reducing/increasing friction.

copy.en:
Why is it easier to carry a heavy sack than to drag it?

Dragging creates friction between the sack and the ground, resisting your pull! When you carry it, that sliding friction is gone. You just have to lift the weight against gravity instead!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas madaling buhatin ang mabigat na sako kaysa kaladkarin?

Ang pagkaladkad ay lumilikha ng friction sa pagitan ng sako at lupa, na humahadlang sa galaw! Kapag binuhat mo, mawawala ang friction na iyon. Kailangan mo lang itaas ang bigat laban sa gravity!
copy.bis:
Nganong mas sayon buhaton ang bug-at nga sako kaysa guyoron?

Ang pagguyod naghimo og friction tali sa sako ug yuta, nga mosupak sa imong pull! Kung buhaton nimo, mawala kining friction. Kinahanglan na lang nimo isakwat ang bug-at batok sa gravity!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: blocking heat inside coolers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes styrofoam as blocking heat, which is an example of insulation, but it does not identify or distinguish conduction, convection, or radiation, nor does it present an advantageous/disadvantageous example of any specific heat transfer mechanism. It only mentions blocking heat generally, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: tiny air pockets
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air pockets as the reason for insulation, which touches on the idea that trapped air reduces heat transfer, but it does not explain the processes of convection or conduction using the particle model. No particle-level explanation is given, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Styrofoam is full of tiny air pockets, making it super good at blocking heat inside coolers!
copy.tl: Ang styrofoam ay punong-puno ng maliliit na air pockets, kaya magaling itong pumigil sa init sa loob ng mga cooler!
copy.bis: Ang styrofoam puno sa gagmay nga air pockets, busa maayo kaayo kini mopugong sa kainit sa sulod sa mga cooler!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In cool highland places such as Baguio and other mountain areas!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card states where fog is common but does not teach identification of weather characteristics (temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, rain, cloud cover). Fog is a form of cloud cover, but the card does not present it as a characteristic or explain how to identify it.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In cool highland places such as Baguio and other mountain areas!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about fog location, not instruction on observing/recording weather changes or describing types/patterns of weather. It does not support the skill of observing or recording weather over time.

copy.en:
Where is fog most common in the Philippines?

In cool highland places such as Baguio and other mountain areas!
copy.tl:
Saan madalas magkaambon sa Pilipinas?

Sa malalamig na lugar tulad ng Baguio at iba pang kabundukan!
copy.bis:
Asa kasagaran adunay gabon sa Pilipinas?

Sa bugnaw nga mga dapit sama sa Baguio ug uban pang kabukiran!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Both are made of tiny water droplets, but fog is thicker and harder to see through than the thinner mist!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes fog and mist as weather phenomena but does not teach any of the listed weather characteristics (air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, cloud cover). It only distinguishes two types of visible moisture, which is not a characteristic used to describe weather.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Both are made of tiny water droplets, but fog is thicker and harder to see through than the thinner mist!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and record changes in the weather during a day or over some days and describe the different types and patterns of weather in the local area
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not involve observing or recording changes in weather over time, nor does it describe types and patterns of weather in the local area. Fog and mist are specific phenomena, not general weather types or patterns, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
What is the difference between fog and mist?

Both are made of tiny water droplets, but fog is thicker and harder to see through than the thinner mist!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng fog at mist?

Pareho silang gawa sa maliliit na patak ng tubig, pero mas makapal ang fog kaya mas mahirap makakita kaysa sa manipis na mist!
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa fog ug mist?

Pareho silang hinimo sa gagmay nga tinulo sa tubig, apan mas baga ang fog mao nga mas lisod makakita kaysa sa nipis nga mist!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Artificial food colorings are carefully tested by food safety authorities like the FDA!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses food coloring safety regulation, not local community issues/concerns or how science addresses them (e.g., waste treatment). It shares the broad theme of science addressing safety but does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Artificial food colorings are carefully tested by food safety authorities like the FDA!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions food colorings (materials) but does not describe chemical properties such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. It is about safety testing, not chemical properties.

copy.en: Artificial food colorings are carefully tested by food safety authorities like the FDA! They are only allowed in specific amounts to make sure they are totally safe to eat.
copy.tl: Ang mga artipisyal na food coloring ay maingat na sinusuri ng food safety authorities tulad ng FDA! Pinapayagan lang sila sa tiyak na dami para siguradong ligtas kainin.
copy.bis: Ang mga artipisyal nga food coloring giduso og maayo sa food safety authorities sama sa FDA! Tugotan lang sila sa piho nga kantidad aron masiguro nga luwas kaonon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: dates — the fruit of a palm tree — and walnuts, a kind of seed
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions fruit and seed, which are plant parts, but the competency specifically targets outer parts (leaves, roots, stems) and their role in water and nutrient uptake. The card provides no information about these structures or their functions, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: This sweet Filipino dessert, food for the gods, is made from dates — the fruit of a palm tree — and walnuts, a kind of seed.
copy.tl: Ang matamis na panghimagas na food for the gods ay gawa sa datiles — bunga ng palmera — at walnut, na isang uri ng buto.
copy.bis: Ang tam-is nga panghimagas nga food for the gods hinimo sa datiles — bunga sa palmera — ug walnut, nga usa ka matang sa liso.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: If brakes are wet, friction is weaker and it takes longer to stop!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes friction slowing a bike and notes that wet brakes reduce friction, but it does not demonstrate friction producing heat nor investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction as a general concept. It only gives a single example of reduced friction, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The friction between them slows and stops the bike.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions friction and its effect on stopping, but it does not involve planning or carrying out a scientific investigation, nor does it compare different surfaces and their effect on frictional force. It is only a descriptive example of friction, not an investigation.

copy.en:
How do bike brakes use friction to stop?

A rubber pad presses the wheel! The friction between them slows and stops the bike. If brakes are wet, friction is weaker and it takes longer to stop!
copy.tl:
Paano gumagamit ang preno ng bisikleta ng friction para tumigil?

May goma na dumidiin sa gulong! Ang friction sa pagitan nila ang nagpapabagal at nagpapatigil. Kapag basa ang preno, mas mahina ang friction at mas matagal tumigil!
copy.bis:
Unsaon paggamit sa preno sa bisikleta sa friction aron mohunong?

Adunay goma nga modiin sa ligid! Ang friction tali nila ang magpahinay ug magpahunong. Kung basa ang preno, mas huyang ang friction ug mas dugay mohunong!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lipote is a native Philippine forest fruit
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a fruit and its use, but does not address outer plant parts (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in obtaining water and nutrients.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Lipote is a native Philippine forest fruit
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single plant example in a forest habitat, but the competency requires making a list or table of animals and plants in a particular habitat; the card does not provide the required list/table format or multiple examples.

copy.en: Lipote is a native Philippine forest fruit with small, sweet-sour purple berries — it grows wild and is often made into jam or juice.
copy.tl: Ang lipote ay katutubong prutas ng gubat sa Pilipinas na may maliliit na maasim-tamis na bungang kulay-ube — madalas gawing jam o juice.
copy.bis: Ang lipote usa ka lumad nga bunga sa lasang sa Pilipinas nga adunay gagmay, aslom-tam-is nga lila nga bunga — kasagaran gihimong jam o juice.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Whole mammoths have been found frozen in ice, preserving even their fur and flesh!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how fossils can be used for dating the age of rocks and sediments
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a fossil preservation fact (frozen mammoths) but does not address how fossils are used for dating rocks and sediments. No mention of dating, age, or geological context.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Whole mammoths have been found frozen in ice, preserving even their fur and flesh!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to explain how lines of evidence, such as fossils, biogeography, and comparative morphology, support the occurrence of evolution
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a fossil (mammoth) as evidence of past life, but does not explain how fossils support evolution, nor does it discuss biogeography, comparative morphology, or any evolutionary mechanism. It is only a factual example of fossil preservation.

copy.en:
What happens to mammoths in very cold places?

Whole mammoths have been found frozen in ice, preserving even their fur and flesh!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa mga mammoth sa napakalamig na lugar?

May mga buong mammoth na natuklasan na nakabaon sa yelo, kaya napreserba pati balahibo at laman!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa mga mammoth sa bugnaw kaayo nga mga dapit?

Adunay tibuok mammoth nga nakit-an nga gibagtok sa yelo, napreserba bisan ang balahibo ug unod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a leaf left an imprint in rock
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how fossils can be used for dating the age of rocks and sediments
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a leaf imprint in rock, illustrating fossil formation, but does not address using fossils to date the age of rocks and sediments. It shares the topic of fossils but provides no direct instructional support for the dating competency.

copy.en: Long ago, a leaf left an imprint in rock, letting us see the exact shape of ancient plants today!
copy.tl: Noong unang panahon, nag-iwan ng tatak sa bato ang isang dahon, kaya nakikita natin ang hugis ng mga sinaunang halaman!
copy.bis: Kaniadto, ang usa ka dahon nagbilin og patik sa bato, busa makita nato ang porma sa mga karaang tanom!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: scratching for food like worms and grains
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that chickens eat worms and grains, which implies an omnivorous diet, but it does not explicitly group chickens as herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources to classify animals. It only provides a diet fact without the grouping action required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In free-range farming, chickens roam the yard freely
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a farming yard as a habitat and chickens as animals, but it does not make a list or table of animals and plants in a named habitat. The format-required list/table is absent, so it cannot directly support this competency.

copy.en: In free-range farming, chickens roam the yard freely, scratching for food like worms and grains.
copy.tl: Sa free-range na pag-aalaga, malayang naglalakad ang manok sa bakuran para humukay ng pagkain gaya ng uod at butil.
copy.bis: Sa free-range nga pag-atiman, gawasnon nga molakaw ang manok sa nataran aron mangita og pagkaon sama sa ulod ug lugas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Almost all of Earth's water is salty seawater — less than 3 percent is fresh water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify what proportion of the Earth's surface is covered with water as opposed to land
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the proportion of Earth's water that is fresh vs. salt, not the proportion of Earth's surface covered by water as opposed to land. It does not support the competency's specific skill of identifying surface water coverage.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Almost all of Earth's water is salty seawater — less than 3 percent is fresh water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water globally but does not identify local landforms or bodies of water, nor describe their influence on living and non-living components. It is only tangentially related to the topic of bodies of water.

copy.en:
How much of Earth's water is actually fresh and drinkable?

Almost all of Earth's water is salty seawater — less than 3 percent is fresh water, and most of that is locked in ice and glaciers!
copy.tl:
Magkano sa tubig ng Mundo ang talagang tabang at maiinom?

Halos lahat ng tubig sa Mundo ay maalat na tubig-dagat — wala pang 3 porsyento ang tabang (fresh) na tubig, at karamihan pa nito ay nakatago sa yelo at glacier!
copy.bis:
Pila sa tubig sa Kalibutan ang tinuod nga tab-ang ug mainom?

Halos tanang tubig sa Kalibutan parat nga tubig-dagat — ubos sa 3 porsyento ang tab-ang (fresh) nga tubig, ug kadaghanan niini natago sa yelo ug glacier!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An eraser creates high friction when rubbed on paper
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that an eraser uses friction to lift graphite, but it does not involve planning or carrying out an investigation, nor does it address how different surfaces affect the size of frictional forces.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An eraser creates high friction when rubbed on paper
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions friction but does not demonstrate friction producing heat, nor does it investigate ways of reducing or increasing friction.

copy.en:
How does an eraser remove pencil marks?

An eraser creates high friction when rubbed on paper — the friction lifts graphite particles off the paper and they stick to the soft eraser!
copy.tl:
Paano nabubura ng pambura ang marka ng lapis?

Ang pambura ay gumagawa ng mataas na friction kapag kinuskos sa papel — ang friction ay nag-aangat ng mga particle ng graphite mula sa papel at dinidikit ang mga ito sa malambot na pambura!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtangtang sa pambura sa marka sa lapis?

Ang pambura nagabuhat og taas nga friction kon gikiskis sa papel — ang friction nagakuha sa mga particle sa graphite gikan sa papel ug nagadikit kini sa malambot nga pambura!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction, which is a fact about reducing friction, but it does not demonstrate how friction produces heat nor does it investigate ways of reducing/increasing friction. It only mentions one example without any investigation or demonstration of heat production.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a comparison of friction types but does not plan or carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on frictional forces. It provides no experimental procedure, variables, or measurement, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Why is it easier to move a box with wheels?

Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction! That's why a box with wheels is easier to move.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas madaling ihatod ang kahon na may gulong?

Mas maliit ang rolling friction kaysa sliding friction! Kaya mas madaling ihatod ang kahon na may gulong.
copy.bis:
Nganong mas sayon ihatod ang kahon nga adunay ligid?

Mas gamay ang rolling friction kaysa sliding friction! Mao nga sayon ihatod ang kahon nga adunay ligid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Steel train wheels on steel rails have very low rolling friction
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about low rolling friction but does not involve planning or carrying out a scientific investigation, nor does it compare different surfaces. It only touches on the topic of friction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Steel train wheels on steel rails have very low rolling friction
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions low rolling friction, which is an example of reducing friction, but it does not demonstrate friction producing heat nor investigate ways of reducing/increasing friction. It provides no instructional support for the competency's actions.

copy.en: Steel train wheels on steel rails have very low rolling friction — that's why trains move heavy freight much more efficiently than trucks on roads!
copy.tl: Ang mga gulong ng tren na bakal sa mga riles na bakal ay may napakababang rolling friction — kaya mas epektibo ng mga tren sa paglipat ng mabibigat na kargamento kaysa sa mga trak!
copy.bis: Ang mga ligid sa tren nga bakal sa mga riles nga bakal adunay gamay kaayo nga rolling friction — mao nga mas epektibo ang mga tren sa pagdala sa mabug-at nga karga kaysa sa mga trak!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It just removes heat from inside and dumps that heat out the back!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses heat removal but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature, which is the core of G7-F-8.

copy.bis: Ang temperatura ang modesisyon! Kon dili pa moabot sa 0°C, makita nimo ang yamog. Apan kon mokunhod sa 0°C o ubos pa, frost crystals ang motungha sa balili.

Ang buckminsterfullerene (C60) usa ka molecule nga adunay 60 carbon atoms nga naka-arrange sama sa soccer ball! Kini usa sa unang nanomaterial nga gigamit sa materials science research.

Walang bibig o tiyan ang fungi, kaya sa halip, ang buong katawan nito ang gumagana parang tiyan na nasa labas para tumunaw ng pagkain.

Ang fungi walay baba o tiyan, mao nga hinuon, ang tibuok lawas niini molihok sama sa tiyan nga naa sa gawas aron tunawon ang pagkaon.

copy.bis: Adunay uhong nga luwas ug masustansyang kan-on, sama sa oyster mushroom nga kanunay lutoon nga lami nga sud-an!

How do fungi eat their food?

Fungi don't swallow food. Their hyphae release chemicals that dissolve food OUTSIDE the body, then soak up the nutrients — like having a stomach on the outside!
copy.tl:
Paano kumakain ang fungi?

Hindi lumulunok ng pagkain ang fungi. Naglalabas ang hyphae nito ng kemikal na tumutunaw sa pagkain sa LABAS ng katawan, tapos sinisipsip ang sustansya — para silang tiyan na nasa labas!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagkaon sa fungi?

Wala motunlo og pagkaon ang fungi. Ang hyphae niini mubuga og kemikal nga motunaw sa pagkaon sa GAWAS sa lawas, dayon mosuyop sa sustansya — murag tiyan nga anaa sa gawas!

Being thin lets a hypha soak up more food through its surface, and squeeze into the tiniest cracks in soil or wood.
copy.tl:
Bakit napakanipis ng sinulid ng fungi?

Dahil manipis, mas madaling sumipsip ng pagkain ang hyphae at makasingit pa sa pinakamaliliit na butas ng lupa o kahoy.
copy.bis:
Nganong nipis kaayo ang hilo sa fungi?

Tungod kay nipis, mas sayon sa hypha nga mosuyop og pagkaon ug makasulod pa sa pinakagamay nga liki sa yuta o kahoy.

A mushroom has three main parts: the cap on top, the stalk below, and the gills under the cap, where its spores are made.

Ang kabute ay may tatlong pangunahing bahagi: ang takip sa itaas, ang tangkay sa ibaba, at ang mga gill sa ilalim ng takip kung saan ginagawa ang mga spore.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mga bahin sa kabute?

Ang kabute adunay tulo ka nag-unang bahin: ang takup sa taas, ang tangkay sa ubos, ug ang mga gill sa ilalom sa takup diin gihimo ang mga spore.

copy.en:

During World War II, scientists grew Penicillium chrysogenum in huge fermentation tanks, mass-producing penicillin for millions of wounded soldiers.
copy.tl:
Paano naging marami ang penicillin?

Noong World War II, nagpalaki ang mga siyentipiko ng produksyon ng penicillin gamit ang Penicillium chrysogenum sa malalaking tanke — nakatulong ito sa milyun-milyong sugatang sundalo.
copy.bis:
Giunsa nadaghan ang penicillin?

Sa panahon sa World War II, gipadaghan sa mga siyentipiko ang produksyon sa penicillin gamit ang Penicillium chrysogenum sa dagkong tanke — nakatabang kini sa milyun-milyong samdan nga sundalo.
